facts.text: Orange Soil Discovery Site was deployed at Taurus-Littrow during Apollo 17 in 1972.

At Shorty Crater, Schmitt — the only geologist to walk on the Moon — discovered orange soil: tiny beads of volcanic glass erupted 3.7 billion years ago. One of the most important geological finds of the programme.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.
The orange glass beads proved the Moon had volcanic fire-fountain eruptions 3.7 billion years ago and contained volatile elements that changed theories about the Moon's formation and water content.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Taurus-Littrow.

Samples of the orange soil (sample 74220) remain among the most studied lunar materials; recent analysis revealed they contain water trapped in volcanic glass, reshaping theories about the Moon's interior.
